newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Relieved Tokyo leads Asian market surge.
newsitem.headline: Relieved Tokyo leads Asian market surge.

text.p: A relieved Tokyo lead a surge by Asian markets on Friday, with the Nikkei closing nearly two percent higher after the settlement of September futures and options went off without a hitch.

Hong Kong closed up more than one percent on a strong stock performance by the colony's major bank and Thai stocks rose for the third straight day with help from a private fund. Only Seoul, Manila and Bombay declined.
Asia's strongest market was Tokyo, where the key 225-share Nikkei average was up 398.71 points or 1.95 percent to close at 20,842.64. December futures jumped 270 points to end at 20,870.
"The settlement that we were worried about finished without any problems and that relieved market participants," said Masayuki Matsumoto, an analyst at Dai-Ichi Securities.
"I expect a very firm tone in the market from next week," said Shunichi Ishimura, general manager of the equities department at Nomura Securities.
Late buying propelled Hong Kong stocks to a sharply higher close, with record highs in HSBC Holdings and Henderson Land shares buoying the Hang Seng index through resistance.
The Hang Seng index closed above 11,300 points at 11,369.04, up 117.32 points or 1.04 percent.
"People were buying more aggressively in the afternoon and this pushed prices up," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities.
HSBC and Henderson Land both closed at record highs.
Thai stocks, rendered directionless by profit-taking earlier in the day, ended the week higher as speculators and a support fund bought stocks, brokers said.
The SET index, in the negative zone most of the day, began rising steadily in the afternoon and closed up 13.44 points or 1.31 percent at 1,039.65.

Taiwan share prices closed higher despite news that Chiang Ping-kun, chairman of the cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development said it was time for local businessmen to slow investment in China.
The index ended up 45.95 points or 0.72 percent at an intraday high of 6,471.63.
Seoul stocks closed sharply lower as heavily index-weighted KEPCO and Samsung Electronics tumbled and brokers said the consolidation would continue next week.
The composite stock index shed 12.38 points or 1.55 percent to provisionally close at 785.19.
The Australian share market rose rapidly in the last hour of trading to close barely a whisker off the day's highs. The All Ordinaries index closed up 15.7 points or 0.70 percent at 2,252.3.

New Zealand shares closed flat in modest trading, deflated by the Reserve Bank announcing no room for easing monetary policy, dealers said. The NZSE-40 capital index finished up 1.67 points or 0.08 percent to close at 2,213.90.
Manila shares closed slightly lower on Friday in the absence of fresh incentives for investors. The main index dropped 0.88 points or 0.03 percent to 3,193.68.

Kuala Lumpur shares finished the week mixed, with blue chips modestly higher, but secondary issues down on profit-taking. The Composite Index rose 4.05 points or 0.36 percent to 1,117.55. The Second Board index fell 1.79 points to 572.24.

SIMEX October Brent futures last traded at $24.12 per barrel, up 25 cents from London's Thursday settlement of $23.87. They were spurred by a firm NYMEX market and the increased tensions surrounding Iraq.

The dollar dipped against the yen in late Tokyo trade after the release of Japan's second quarter growth data, which was mostly within expectations. At 1042 GMT, the dollar was trading at 110.24/0.34 yen and 1.5120/25 marks.
Hong Kong gold bullion ended at US$382.50/383.00 an ounce against New York's US$382.45/95 close on Thursday.
